steps.title: Read the denial and the deadline
steps.detail: Read the denial letter: Home health physical therapy, 12 visits over 6 weeks, denied on 2026-10-20; appeal by 2026-12-24.

steps.title: Pull supporting notes from the records
steps.detail: Pulled 7 relevant items from the records (visits, results, medicines). Nothing is added that isn't on file.

steps.title: Get a letter of medical necessity from the doctor
steps.detail: Called Harbor Light Internal Medicine at (555) 010-0211: pressed 4 (medical records), then transferred to the doctor's medical assistant, waited 15 minutes on hold, reached Rob, the doctor's medical assistant. The doctor will sign the letter and the office will fax it. Reference R-17296.

steps.title: Match the evidence to the plan's rules
steps.detail: Mapped 16 pieces of evidence to the plan's 4 rules: 4 met, 0 partly.

steps.title: Write the appeal
steps.detail: Appeal letter drafted, with the doctor's letter, records and a criteria table attached.

steps.title: Stress-test the appeal
steps.detail: Stress-tested: the insurer-side reviewer went over it 2 times; the writer answered its objections in 1 revision, and the last review found no reason to deny.

steps.title: Fax it to the plan and confirm it arrived

rules.rule: The member is homebound: leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort.
A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy.
Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep the member's function.
The services are reasonable and necessary for the member's condition.

review.original:
I'm appealing the denial of home health physical therapy, which was denied because the plan says it isn't medically necessary.
My doctor, Dr. Samuel Okafor (Harbor Light Internal Medicine), has written the enclosed letter of medical necessity. The enclosed records show the history behind the request. Each of the plan's coverage criteria is answered in the enclosed table.

Please send me the plan's decision in writing, and a copy of the criteria used.

objections.rule: The member is homebound: leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort.
objections.reason: The letter does not state that leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort or cite any evidence of homebound status.
objections.needs: A statement that the member needs a walker and help to leave home and that it is a taxing effort, citing the 2026-10-10 physical therapy evaluation

objections.rule: A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy.
objections.reason: The letter does not state that a doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy or identify the signed plan of care.
objections.needs: A statement that Dr. Samuel Okafor certified a plan of care for physical therapy, citing the 2026-10-14 signed home health plan of care for 12 visits

objections.rule: Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep the member's function.
objections.reason: The letter does not explain why skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep function or cite evidence of need.
objections.needs: A statement that balance and walking declined after the fall and skilled therapy can restore them, citing the 2026-10-10 physical therapy evaluation

objections.rule: The services are reasonable and necessary for the member's condition.
objections.reason: The letter does not explain why home services are reasonable and necessary or why outpatient therapy is not suitable.
objections.needs: A statement that outpatient therapy is not safe due to fall risk on stairs and in transit, citing the 2026-10-14 doctor's note

revision.body:
Dear Appeals Unit at Bluewater Health,

I am appealing the denial of home health physical therapy denied on 2026-10-20. My member ID is BWM-77031882 and my case number is SIM-PA-20431.

The denial states I am not homebound and skilled therapy in my home is not medically necessary. I meet each coverage rule for the reasons below:

1. I am homebound: leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort. My physical therapy evaluation on 2026-10-10 states I need a walker and one person's help to leave home and that leaving home takes a taxing effort.

2. A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy. My home health plan of care for physical therapy, 12 visits, was certified and signed by Dr. Samuel Okafor of Harbor Light Internal Medicine on 2026-10-14.

3. Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep my function. My physical therapy evaluation on 2026-10-10 states my balance and walking have declined since the fall and skilled therapy can restore them.

4. The services are reasonable and necessary for my condition. The certified plan of care signed by Dr. Samuel Okafor prescribes 12 visits of physical therapy. The evaluation documents the decline in balance and walking and that skilled therapy can restore them. Dr. Okafor's note on 2026-10-14 also states outpatient therapy isn't safe for me right now because of fall risk on stairs and in transit.

Enclosed are my medical records and the denial notice. Please send me your written decision and a copy of the criteria used.
